paragraphs: Here's what I see, friend. Saul gets crowned, and some people grumble that he can't save anybody (1 Samuel 10:27). Then a real crisis hits, and the Spirit of God rushes upon Saul (1 Samuel 11:6). The doubters had a question, and God answered it with a rescue.

Now look at what Saul does with the win. The people want to put the grumblers to death, and Saul says, "No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel." (1 Samuel 11:13) He had every reason to settle the score, and he handed the credit to the LORD instead. I'll be honest, I've held a grudge over a cookie crumb, so that is a whole other level.

So here's the lesson to take with you. When God moves, the glory goes to Him, and mercy goes to the people who doubted. Pride says, "Look what I did." The LORD's people say, "Look what He did." Keep that one in your apron pocket, and notice that Saul's story isn't done yet.
